   * 1. Summary: Executes an inertial slide in the given direction, returning the appropriate MoveResult.
   * 2. Algorithm: 
   *    1. pos = gameBoard.player.position
   *    2. dRow, dCol = direction deltas
   *    3. current = pos. collectedGems = [], collectedExtraLives = []
   *    4. Loop:
   *       a. next = current.offsetByOrNull1(dRow, dCol, gameBoard.numRows, gameBoard.numCols)
   *       b. If next is null OR getCell(next) is Wall: break (stop before obstacle/boundary)
   *       c. cell = getCell(next)
   *       d. If cell is StopCell: current = next; break (stop exactly on StopCell)
   *       e. If cell is Mine: return Dead(minePosition=next). Player stays at pos. Board unchanged.
   *       f. If cell is Gem/ExtraLife: add to respective list. Remove item from board. current = next.
   *       g. Else (Empty): current = next.
   *    5. If current == pos: return Invalid()
   *    6. Else: Create Alive(pos=newPosition=current, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives). Update gameBoard.player.position to current. Return Alive.
   * 3. Related Features: gameBoard, player, board, movement logic, collection tracking
   * 4. Related Classes: GameBoard, Position, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Player, Cell, Wall, StopCell, Mine, Gem, ExtraLife
   * 5. Input: direction (Direction): UP, DOWN, LEFT, or RIGHT.
   * 6. Output: MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid)
   * 7. Pre-condition: gameBoard is initialized, player exists, direction is valid.
   * 8. Post-condition: Player position updated only on successful slides. Board modified (items removed) only on Alive. Dead/Invalid leave board and player unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT

  public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction)
  {
      // 1. pos = gameBoard.player.position
      Position pos = gameBoard.getPlayer().getPosition();
      
      // 2. dRow, dCol = direction deltas
      int dRow = direction.getDRow();
      int dCol = direction.getDCol();
      
      // 3. current = pos. collectedGems = [], collectedExtraLives = []
      Position current = pos;
      EList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<>();
      EList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<>();
      
      // 4. Loop:
      while (true) {
          // a. next = current.offsetByOrNull1(dRow, dCol, gameBoard.numRows, gameBoard.numCols)
          Position next = current.offsetByOrNull1(dRow, dCol, gameBoard.getNumRows(), gameBoard.getNumCols());
          
          // b. If next is null OR getCell(next) is Wall: break
          if (next == null || gameBoard.getCell(next) instanceof Wall) {
              break;
          }
          
          // c. cell = getCell(next)
          Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(next);
          
          // d. If cell is StopCell: current = next; break
          if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
              current = next;
              break;
          }
          
          // e. If cell is Mine: return Dead(minePosition=next). Player stays at pos. Board unchanged.
          if (cell instanceof Mine) {
              return Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createDead(next);
          }
          
          // f. If cell is Gem/ExtraLife: add to respective list. Remove item from board. current = next.
          if (cell instanceof Gem) {
              collectedGems.add(next);
              gameBoard.setCell(next, null);
          } else if (cell instanceof ExtraLife) {
              collectedExtraLives.add(next);
              gameBoard.setCell(next, null);
          }
          
          // g. Else (Empty): current = next.
          current = next;
      }
      
      // 5. If current == pos: return Invalid()
      if (current.equals(pos)) {
          return Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createInvalid();
      }
      
      // 6. Else: Create Alive(pos=newPosition=current, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives). Update gameBoard.player.position to current. Return Alive.
      Alive alive = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createAlive(current, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
      gameBoard.getPlayer().setPosition(current);
      return alive;
  }

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * 1. Summary: Reverses a previously executed Alive move, restoring board state and player position.
   * 2. Algorithm: 
   *    1. Assert prevMove is instance of Alive.

   *    3. For each gemPos in prevMove.collectedGems: Place Gem at gemPos on board.
   *    4. For each extraLifePos in prevMove.collectedExtraLives: Place ExtraLife at extraLifePos. Trigger life reversal (-1 life).
   *    5. Clear collectedGems and collectedExtraLives in prevMove.
   * 3. Related Features: gameBoard, player, move result data, life management hooks
   * 4. Related Classes: GameBoard, Alive, Position, Gem, ExtraLife, GameState (lives)

   * 6. Output: None (void)
   * 7. Pre-condition: prevMove represents a valid, completed Alive move.
   * 8. Post-condition: Player position restored, collected items re-spawned on board, extra life effects reversed.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"

  public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove)
  {
      // 1. Assert prevMove is instance of Alive.
      if (!(prevMove instanceof Alive)) {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("prevMove must be an instance of Alive.");
      }
      Alive alive = (Alive) prevMove;
      
      // 2. gameBoard.player.position = prevMove.origPosition
      gameBoard.getPlayer().setPosition(alive.getOrigPosition());
      
      // 3. For each gemPos in prevMove.collectedGems: Place Gem at gemPos on board.
      for (Position gemPos : alive.getCollectedGems()) {
          gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new Gem());
      }
      
      // 4. For each extraLifePos in prevMove.collectedExtraLives: Place ExtraLife at extraLifePos. Trigger life reversal (-1 life).
      for (Position extraLifePos : alive.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
          gameBoard.setCell(extraLifePos, new ExtraLife());
          gameBoard.setLives(gameBoard.getLives() - 1);
      }
      
      // 5. Clear collectedGems and collectedExtraLives in prevMove.
      alive.getCollectedGems().clear();
      alive.getCollectedExtraLives().clear();
  }

## EMF Coding Style

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::decreaseNumLives
Summary: Decreases the number of lives by a specified delta.
Algorithm: this.numLives -= delta; return this.numLives;
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta (int): Amount to decrease. Must be positive.
Output: int: Updated number of lives.
Pre-condition: numLives >= 0 (unless in unlimited mode where it stays < 0). delta >= 0.
Post-condition: numLives reduced by delta. Returns new value.

GameState::hasWon
Summary: Checks if the player has met the win condition.
Algorithm: return this.getNumGems() == 0;
Related Features: getNumGems
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if won.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns win status.

GameState::decrementNumLives
Summary: Decreases lives by exactly 1.
Algorithm: return this.decreaseNumLives(1)
Related Features: decreaseNumLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Updated number of lives.
Pre-condition: Same as decreaseNumLives.
Post-condition: numLives decreased by 1.

GameState::hasUnlimitedLives
Summary: Checks if unlimited lives mode is active.
Algorithm: return this.numLives < 0;
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if unlimited.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns mode status.

GameState::getGameBoardView
Summary: Provides access to the view component responsible for rendering the game board.
Algorithm: return this.gameBoardView
Related Features: gameBoardView (inferred association)
Related Classes: GameBoardView
Input: None.
Output: GameBoardView: The view instance bound to this state.
Pre-condition: View is initialized.
Post-condition: Returns view reference without side effects.

GameState::getNumGems
Summary: Delegates to GameBoard to retrieve the count of remaining gems.
Algorithm: return this.gameBoard.getNumGems()
Related Features: gameBoard
Related Classes: GameBoard
Input: None.
Output: int: Remaining gems count.
Pre-condition: Board initialized.
Post-condition: Returns current gem count.

GameState::increaseNumLives
Summary: Increases lives by a delta. Used when collecting ExtraLife items.
Algorithm: if this.hasUnlimitedLives(): return this.numLives; this.numLives += delta; return this.numLives;
Related Features: numLives, hasUnlimitedLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta (int): Amount to increase.
Output: int: Updated lives.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Lives increased. If unlimited, remains negative.

GameState::incrementNumDeaths
Summary: Increments the death counter by 1.
Algorithm: this.numDeaths++; return this.numDeaths;
Related Features: numDeaths
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Updated death count.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: numDeaths increased by 1.

GameState::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has met the lose condition.
Algorithm: if this.hasUnlimitedLives(): return false; else: return this.getnumLives() <= 0;
Related Features: hasUnlimitedLives, getnumLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if lost.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns accurate loss status.

GameState::getScore
Summary: Calculates the current score based on the official formula.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: gameBoard, initialNumOfGems, getNumGems, moveStack, numDeaths, numMoves
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveStack
Input: None.
Output: int: Calculated score.
Pre-condition: All state variables initialized.
Post-condition: Returns score per formula. Negative scores clamped to 0.

GameState::incrementNumMoves
Summary: Increments the move counter by 1.
Algorithm: this.numMoves++; return this.numMoves;
Related Features: numMoves
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Updated move count.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: numMoves increased by 1.

GameState::getnumLives

Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Current lives or MAX_VALUE.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns effective lives count.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::decreaseNumLives
Summary: Decreases the number of lives by a specified delta.
Algorithm: if this.numLives < 0: return this.numLives; this.numLives -= delta; return this.numLives;
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta (int): Amount to decrease. Must be non-negative.
Output: int: Updated number of lives.
Pre-condition: delta >= 0.
Post-condition: If in unlimited mode (numLives < 0), numLives remains unchanged. Otherwise, numLives is reduced by delta and the new value is returned.

GameState::hasWon
Summary: Checks if the player has met the win condition.
Algorithm: return this.getNumGems() == 0;
Related Features: getNumGems
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if won.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns win status.

GameState::decrementNumLives
Summary: Decreases lives by exactly 1.
Algorithm: return this.decreaseNumLives(1)
Related Features: decreaseNumLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Updated number of lives.
Pre-condition: Same as decreaseNumLives.
Post-condition: numLives decreased by 1.

GameState::hasUnlimitedLives
Summary: Checks if unlimited lives mode is active.
Algorithm: return this.numLives < 0;
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if unlimited.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns mode status.

GameState::getGameBoardView
Summary: Provides access to the view component responsible for rendering the game board.
Algorithm: return this.gameBoardView
Related Features: gameBoardView (inferred association)
Related Classes: GameBoardView
Input: None.
Output: GameBoardView: The view instance bound to this state.
Pre-condition: View is initialized.
Post-condition: Returns view reference without side effects.

GameState::getNumGems
Summary: Delegates to GameBoard to retrieve the count of remaining gems.
Algorithm: return this.gameBoard.getNumGems()
Related Features: gameBoard
Related Classes: GameBoard
Input: None.
Output: int: Remaining gems count.
Pre-condition: Board initialized.
Post-condition: Returns current gem count.

GameState::increaseNumLives
Summary: Increases lives by a delta. Used when collecting ExtraLife items.
Algorithm: if this.hasUnlimitedLives(): return this.numLives; this.numLives += delta; return this.numLives;
Related Features: numLives, hasUnlimitedLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta (int): Amount to increase.
Output: int: Updated lives.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Lives increased. If unlimited, remains negative.

GameState::incrementNumDeaths
Summary: Increments the death counter by 1.
Algorithm: this.numDeaths++; return this.numDeaths;
Related Features: numDeaths
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Updated death count.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: numDeaths increased by 1.

GameState::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has met the lose condition.
Algorithm: return !this.hasUnlimitedLives() && this.numLives <= 0;
Related Features: hasUnlimitedLives, numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if lost.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns accurate loss status based on life count and mode.

GameState::getScore
Summary: Calculates the current score based on the official formula.
Algorithm: int boardSize = this.gameBoard.numRows * this.gameBoard.numCols;
Related Features: gameBoard, initialNumOfGems, getNumGems, moveStack, numDeaths, numMoves
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveStack
Input: None.
Output: int: Calculated score.
Pre-condition: All state variables initialized.
Post-condition: Returns score per formula.

GameState::incrementNumMoves
Summary: Increments the move counter by 1.
Algorithm: this.numMoves++; return this.numMoves;
Related Features: numMoves
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Updated move count.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: numMoves increased by 1.

GameState::getnumLives
Summary: Returns current lives, handling unlimited mode conversion.
Algorithm: if this.numLives < 0: return Integer.MAX_VALUE; else: return this.numLives;
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: int: Current lives or MAX_VALUE.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns effective lives count.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameController::processMove
Summary: Orchestrates move execution, updates game state counters, handles life management, and manages the move stack.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: incrementNumMoves, incrementNumDeaths, decrementNumLives, increaseNumLives, hasWon, hasLost, moveStack, getGameBoardController
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, MoveStack
Input: direction (Direction): Movement direction.
Output: MoveResult: Outcome of the processed move.
Pre-condition: Game is active. State variables are initialized.
Post-condition: Counters updated. MoveStack modified if Alive. Lives adjusted. Win/Loss states evaluated.

GameController::processUndo
Summary: Undoes the last recorded Alive move if available, updating state accordingly.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: moveStack, isEmpty, peek, pop, popCount
Related Classes: GameState, MoveStack, GameBoardController, MoveResult, Alive
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if undo successful, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: MoveStack exists and contains at least one Alive move.
Post-condition: Last Alive move reverted. popCount incremented. numMoves remains unchanged.

Post-condition: Counters updated. MoveStack modified if Alive. Lives adjusted. Win/Loss states evaluated.

Algorithm: 
Related Features: moveStack, isEmpty, peek, pop, popCount
Related Classes: GameState, MoveStack, GameBoardController, MoveResult, Alive
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if undo successful, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: MoveStack exists and contains at least one Alive move.
Post-condition: Last Alive move reverted. popCount incremented. numMoves remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::push
Summary: Adds a move to the top of the stack.
Algorithm: this.moves.add(move);
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: move (MoveResult): The move to record.
Output: void
Pre-condition: move is not null.
Post-condition: move added to stack.

MoveStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the top move. Increments the undo tracker.
Algorithm: if this.isEmpty(): throw EmptyStackException; this.popCount++; return this.moves.remove(this.moves.size() - 1);
Related Features: moves, popCount, isEmpty
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: MoveResult: Removed element.
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: popCount incremented. Top element removed.

MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Checks if the stack contains any recorded moves.
Algorithm: return this.moves.size() == 0;
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: True if empty.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: No state change.

MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the top move without removing it.
Algorithm: if this.isEmpty(): throw EmptyStackException; return this.moves.get(this.moves.size() - 1);
Related Features: moves, isEmpty
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: MoveResult: Top element.
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: No state change.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
EntityCell::setentity
Summary: Places an entity into this cell and updates the entity's owner reference.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: EntityCell.entity, Entity.owner
Related Classes: Entity
Input: newEntity (Entity) - The entity to place in the cell. Must not be null.
Output: Entity - The updated entity reference stored in the cell.
Pre-condition: newEntity is not null. The cell is not already occupied by another entity.
Post-condition: this.entity equals newEntity, and newEntity.owner equals this cell.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary: Reverts a previously executed Alive move, restoring the player position and collected items to the board.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: GameBoard.player, GameBoard.placeEntity()
Related Classes: MoveResult, Alive, Position, Cell
Input: prevMove (MoveResult) - The Alive move result to revert. Must be an Alive instance.
Output: void

Post-condition: Player position restored to origPosition. Collected gems/lives placed back on board. prevMove collection lists cleared.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Position::offsetBy1
Summary: Computes a new Position by adding integer row/column offsets.
Algorithm: return new Position(this.row + dRow, this.col + dCol)
Related Features: Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: None
Input: dRow (int) - Vertical offset.
Output: Position - New coordinates.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returned position reflects arithmetic addition of offsets.

Position::offsetByOrNull1
Summary: Computes an offset position, returning null if the result falls outside board boundaries.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Position.offsetBy1, Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: None
Input: dRow (int), dCol (int) - Offsets.
Output: Position or null
Pre-condition: numRows, numCols > 0.
Post-condition: Returns valid position if within bounds, else null.

Position::offsetBy2
Summary: Computes a new Position by adding a PositionOffset object.
Algorithm: return offsetBy1(offset.dRow, offset.dCol)
Related Features: Position.offsetBy1
Related Classes: PositionOffset
Input: offset (PositionOffset) - Vector containing dRow and dCol. Must not be null.
Output: Position - New coordinates.
Pre-condition: offset is not null.
Post-condition: Returned position reflects addition of offset values.

Position::offsetByOrNull2
Summary: Computes an offset position using a PositionOffset, returning null if out of bounds.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Position.offsetBy2
Related Classes: PositionOffset
Input: offset (PositionOffset) - Offset vector.
Output: Position or null
Pre-condition: numRows, numCols > 0.
Post-condition: Returns valid position if within bounds, else null.
